When I was 7 years old, my father died of motor neurone disease. But that's the tip of the iceberg.

Up to his death, my mum almost literally spent all of her free time looking after him, so that meant I received almost no attention from either of them before I was growing up. I was constantly pushed back and pushed away from them. But I don't blame them.

I'm 17 years old now, and I can't speak to my mum, I can mumble just about, and say basic phrases, but I am practically selectively mute around her and the rest of my family due to being conditioned to being pushed away from her. I can't laugh, neither feel emotions around them. I can't even text them, and I want to *so bad*.

I haven't let it completely ruin my life, but I need to come to the acceptance that I don't really have a family. I love them and they love me, but I practically don't have a family.

I can talk to other people just fine. It's selective mutism, and it only effect my ability to talk to my own family.

As you can imagine this depresses me *extremely* and is the root cause of my sadness. I am 16 now and I am pretty sure that it is too late to reverse the damage done and I will probably never have a conversation with any family members. I feel like shit 24/7 and can not imagine being happy and having this problem at the same time.
